title: Environmental Thermodynamics: The Energetic Logic of a Changing World
content:
Environmental thermodynamics provides a common framework for many
of the complex problems arising from growing environmental pressures and the
challenges of sustainable development, allowing to formulate them in terms of energetic
constraints. We discuss this perspective with three
examples spanning scales from soil pores to the planet. First, we illustrate how microbial
cooperation in soils can shift the feasibility boundaries of organic-matter
oxidation, allowing syntrophic reactions that would otherwise be energetically
inaccessible. Second, we map the hydrologic cycle onto a Rankine engine
whose finite-time operation is scheduled by a self-excited land--atmosphere
oscillator, linking thermodynamic work, hydrologic storage, and rainfall
intermittency. Finally, we present the thermodynamic basis of climate change
and how modern large-scale computation couples to climate, adding to
environmental pressure. Together, these examples show how environmental
thermodynamics can provide a productive framework for interdisciplinary
research and education.
